summary: Verified CORS + Bearer-only auth fixes for the iLoveWorks Capacitor mobile build. Backend tests (23/23 passing) confirm: (a) FastAPI CORS regex correctly echoes capacitor://localhost, ionic://localhost, http://localhost[:port], and both Emergent domains with allow-credentials=true when hitting the backend directly; (b) bogus origins are refused; (c) Bearer-only auth works end-to-end for worker + admin (no cookies required). Frontend E2E in headed browser confirms login stores access_token in localStorage, dashboard loads, /auth/me + /tasks + /time/active + /essentials + /goals all return 200 with Bearer only (cookies cleared), logout clears token, admin login also works.

minor.issue: Emergent Cloudflare/ingress rewrites Access-Control-Allow-Origin to '*' on all responses AND preserves the backend's Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true header on non-OPTIONS responses when a valid origin was sent. Combination is a CORS spec violation for credentialed requests. NOT a functional blocker here because the frontend was intentionally changed to withCredentials=false and uses Bearer. However, if any future call sets withCredentials=true from a browser it will be rejected by the browser.

Returns 404. Admin worker listing lives at /api/workers instead. /app/memory/test_credentials.md documents /api/workers (correct); review_request mentioned /api/users/workers (does not exist). Recommend updating any frontend/docs that reference /api/users/workers.
Endpoint does not exist. Review request mentioned 'trips list' as a regression, but backend has no /api/trips route. Trips tab in UI may render client-side only or use a different path.

action_items: OPTIONAL: If you want the deployment topology to be spec-clean, ask the platform team to stop injecting Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on responses when the upstream (our backend) already sets a specific origin. Current behavior is safe only while frontend keeps withCredentials=false.
Confirm what backend endpoint powers the 'Trips' UI tab; /api/trips is 404. If Trips is expected to fetch data, this will be an integration bug in the mobile build (and possibly web).
Sync /app/memory/test_credentials.md and any Admin UI code to use /api/workers (not /api/users/workers).
critical_code_review_comments: Backend CORS middleware config in /app/backend/server.py (line ~2758) correctly extends allow_origin_regex to include capacitor://localhost and ionic://localhost, anchored with ^...$. Verified via direct request to http://localhost:8001 that all target origins are echoed with credentials=true and evil.example.com is refused.

/app/frontend/src/lib/api.js correctly sets withCredentials=false and attaches Bearer token from localStorage via interceptor. This is the right design for Capacitor webviews given the ingress '*' rewrite.
/app/frontend/.env.production correctly bakes production URL for `yarn build`. .env still points at preview for dev.

AuthContext calls refresh() on mount which triggers a /auth/me before user has token, producing an expected 401 in console. Not a bug but could be silenced by short-circuiting when no localStorage token exists (minor UX polish).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (6/6 flows: worker-login, bearer-only, dashboard-load, multi-endpoint, logout, admin-login)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 6 focused on the Capacitor CORS + Bearer-only auth fix. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_cors_bearer_iter6.py covers both the backend-direct CORS surface (proves regex is correct) and the public URL surface (proves no spec violation on preflight, documents the known ingress rewrite behavior on POSTs). Frontend Bearer-only path was verified by clearing cookies mid-session and re-issuing all critical GETs with only Authorization: Bearer — all returned 200. Two documentation/route mismatches were surfaced: /api/users/workers (404, use /api/workers) and /api/trips (404, no such route).
rca of the issue: Original bug: Xcode/Capacitor iOS build could not talk to backend. Three root causes: (1) FastAPI CORS regex missing capacitor://localhost + ionic://localhost — FIXED in server.py (verified). (2) Frontend axios used withCredentials=true, which forces the browser to enforce strict allow-origin==echo + allow-credentials==true; but Emergent ingress rewrites allow-origin to '*', creating a wildcard+credentials conflict browsers reject — FIXED by switching to withCredentials=false + Bearer token (verified). (3) Production URL not baked into mobile build — FIXED via .env.production. All three fixes verified working in this iteration.
